segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Brocard Axis is the central line connecting the Circumcenter X three and the Symmedian Point X six. It serves as the line of symmetry of the Brocard configuration and is perpendicular to the Lemoine axis.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Because the three Apollonian circles have their centers on the Lemoine axis, their common radical chord is the Brocard axis. The two intersection points of all three Apollonian circles—the First and Second Isodynamic Points X fifteen and X sixteen—lie directly on the Brocard axis.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Segment X three X six is the diameter of the Brocard circle, while X fifteen and X sixteen are mutual inverses in the circumcircle and harmonic conjugates with respect to the Apollonian structure along the Brocard axis.
